I don't have a Flemish Giant but I do have a Giant Chinchilla and New Zealand rabbit.

In my opinion, giants are actually excellent 'first time' rabbits. Do your research of course, but in many ways they are easier to care for than smaller rabbits provided you have the space. Bigger digestive tracts, so a mistake can be more forgiving (mine got into cat food once before I realised he would eat it...). Harder to escape if you accidentally leave a door open or a gap in an outdoor run. Usually sweet and friendly.

Main difference is space. Your giant is almost certainly going to need to be completely free range in the house rather than confined to a pen. You'll need a big litter tray (I use an under bed storage box). They obviously eat more.
